routines.semantics: Begin a backward search on a live DAF, select it, and reset its per-file cursor to just past the last array. It becomes current even when empty.

scenarios.observes: Backward search makes the last array available first, then the first, before exhaustion.
An empty DAF supports beginning and repeating a backward search.
Beginning again on the same handle resets its cursor to just after the last array.
Backward initialization replaces an earlier forward cursor.
Backward starts on independent files retain their own array positions.

routines.edgeAssessment: Prove initialization, replacement of a prior forward search, restart after positioning, empty search and independent positions across files.
routines.errorAssessment: The raw public API excludes closed, foreign and wrong-kind claims before the call. Ordinary empty files support a successful search. Media-read failures are outside the authored intact fixtures.

routines.semantics: Select the owned file, advance to the previous array once, and return whether the result is current. The initialized traced SPICELIB DAFFPA alias preserves the pinned operation and avoids its public shim’s private uninitialized output on early failure.

scenarios.observes: Observe both arrays backward, repeated exhaustion, then a forward step from the endpoint.
No previous arrays exist at any position in the empty file.
A backward step at the fresh forward start is false; forward advancement remains possible.
Interleaved previous calls implicitly select their specified file and retain both saved cursors.
A preceding DAFCS failure propagates before any advancement. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(DAFNOSEARCH).

routines.edgeAssessment: Compare a complete reverse traversal, repeated false after exhaustion, forward recovery, absence before the first array and interleaved files. Each public call consumes one cursor transition. On independently restarted valid two-array searches, the ordinary locked public wrapper and the separately bound initialized routine both returned true/SEGMENT 2, true/SEGMENT 1, false, false.
routines.errorAssessment: A valid owned file with no started search raises DAFNOSEARCH during DAFCS selection. No original-wrapper invocation on an undefined error path is needed.

routines.semantics: Read the toolkit’s current file and return the oldest surviving local DAF token for its native handle. A matching reference already owned by another client is resolved independently in that client.

scenarios.observes: DAFGH returns the active owner after beginning a search, before any array is current.
Current handle identity follows explicit and implicit selections across files.
Two owned opens share a native DAF handle; closing the oldest promotes the surviving token.
Reopening a previously closed label registers a new owner after the remaining alias.
An exhausted search retains its owning DAF handle.

routines.edgeAssessment: Observe selection before positioning, exhaustion, duplicate open/close promotion and moving a reopened workflow label after surviving older claims. Separate native clients exercise process-global current state.
routines.errorAssessment: A current file with no local claim is rejected without creating a token. The toolkit documents DAFNOSEARCH when no search exists. The registered cases also distinguish an active search with no current array. An isolated fresh locked-oracle process observed DAFNOSEARCH, trace dafgh_c --> DAFGH, then failed()==false. This initial-state probe is separate from shared-workflow registration.

routines.semantics: Select the supplied DAF and return the current name with toolkit trailing-blank conversion and strict UTF-8 decoding. namlen is a signed byte capacity including NUL. The default physical capacity is 1001.

scenarios.observes: Read complete and truncated first and last array names with explicit NUL-inclusive capacities.
Name lookups switch active files without advancing either cursor.
Starting a search does not position it on an array yet. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(NOCURRENTARRAY).
The name cannot be read past the final array. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(NOCURRENTARRAY).
Length one cannot accommodate a character and its terminating NUL. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(STRINGTOOSHORT).
A negative logical name capacity receives toolkit length validation. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(STRINGTOOSHORT).
Explicit handle selection precedes name buffer validation. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(DAFNOSEARCH).
Capture the actual missing-array and short-buffer errors on one owner, then read the complete name and summary without resetting its search.

routines.edgeAssessment: Observe prefixes, distinct first/last names, selection across files and true toolkit error precedence. The separate fixture independently verifies a terminal tab and truncated trailing blank.
routines.errorAssessment: NOCURRENTARRAY applies before first and after last position, STRINGTOOSHORT to an active search with length below two, and DAFNOSEARCH to an unstarted search even with insufficient length. The public adapter rejects an invalid/incomplete UTF-8 byte prefix.

routines.semantics: Select the file, obtain ND and NI, read the entire current packed summary into 125 available double words and return an owned byte array of exactly 8*(ND+ceil(NI/2)) native-order bytes.

scenarios.observes: Compare each summary byte for both arrays, including distinct packed body and address words.
Preserve the authored negative body and center integer bits even when their packed double word is a NaN.
Switch between CK and SPK arrays and observe every format-specific summary byte.

routines.semantics: Open an existing native-format DAF with write access and register its native claim as an owner-local public token, resolving mounted virtual paths. Close with DAFCLS.

scenarios.observes: Open a generated SPK for write, navigate its array, close, and reopen the same file for read.
A new write claim is permitted once the prior write claim closes.
An existing writable claim prevents a second write open on the same generated file. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(FILEOPENCONFLICT).
A read claim on an existing generated file prevents a write open. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(FILEOPENCONFLICT).
Opening an existing file for read while it has a write claim produces the actual read/write conflict. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(RWCONFLICT).
Opening a nonexistent file for write does not create a DAF. Actual toolkit diagnostic SPICE(FILENOTFOUND).
Resolve the logical SPK writer path to its unique generated scratch file before a DAF write open.

routines.edgeAssessment: Observe content and dimensions through the writer, a read reopen after close, another writer after close and normalized generated-path aliases. Independently injected registration failure closes the acquired native writer.
routines.errorAssessment: The genuine errors comprise FILENOTFOUND on a missing path, FILEOPENCONFLICT for a writer requested while the file is already open and RWCONFLICT for a reader requested during a live writer. Failure releases all temporary allocations.
routines.fixtureRationale: Each writer case creates its own scratch SPK through actual SPKOPN, SPKW08 and SPKCLS as needed, or deliberately addresses a nonexistent scratch file. No repository binary is opened for write.
routines.cleanup: Explicit DAFCLS releases one registered claim. Success and error finalizers attempt to close remaining DAF/SPK handles and remove physical case scratch directories. The WASM module owns MEMFS files until disposal. Each writable run receives a unique virtual path on a reused module. Node serializes cursor selection and operation under its native lock. WASM releases every temporary acquisition even on failure. A registration error explicitly releases the newly opened writer.
routines.tolerance: Compare exact names, owner relationships, sequence flags, format fields and summary bytes after reopening. Opaque integer representation can differ across processes.

findings.summary: An error issuing an opaque token after a successful C writer open would retain an untracked write claim and prevent reopening.
findings.repair: Close the just-acquired native handle on registration failure. Real native and WASM regressions inject owner registration failure, then reopen the same scratch file for reading.

findings.summary: The same generated path can already exist when a DAF-writing scenario is rerun on a live WASM module with persistent MEMFS.
findings.repair: Scope generated write-open SPKs by the unique run scratch directory. Publish the same generated location for read/write and kernel-load consumers while requiring a scratch reference before write-open. The actual case can be run again without replacing repository fixtures.
